title: الفصل الثاني عشر من الباب الرابع في صفة قلم الحكيم هرمس ابوطاط الذي كتب الصنعة الشريفة . وصنع باقليم الصعيد كنوزا وبرابي ونواويس كاهنية له ولولده . ورصدها ورمزها بهذا القلم . الذي استخرجه من السرب المظلم — Hammer: "SECTION XII. The alphabet of Hermes Abootat the philosopher. … extracted from the regions of darkness, (v. orig. p. 34.)" [Chapter IV, English pp. 6-7]

table: The pen of the sage Hirmis Abū Ṭāṭ (هرمس ابوطاط; Hammer: "Hermes Abootat"). In this file's own paraphrase of the Arabic heading: he wrote on the noble art, made treasures, temples (barābī) and priestly tombs (nawāwīs) in the province of al-Ṣaʿīd for himself and his son, and guarded and encoded them with this pen, which he brought out of the dark tunnel (السرب المظلم). Hammer's English renders the last words "extracted from the regions of darkness". 28 signs in three rows (10, 9, 9), read right to left, each with an Arabic letter printed beneath it, in abjad order from ا to غ; every label was read from the scan and agrees with that order. The ascription to Hermes is the book's.
conventions: Centre-line strokes with the kit pen (5.5), heavier than the print's fine line (about 3-4 units). Small open circles at stroke ends are kit rings, with r set to the centre line of the printed ring (4.5-6.3); the stroke stops at the ring's edge, and the ring is placed where the print has it even where that is not quite on the line of the stroke. Signs that are themselves closed figures (alif's oval, hāʾ's shield, lām's and ghayn's triangles, the oval of bāʾ, khāʾ's bow) are drawn as closed paths, not as rings. The pennant of ṣād is a closed triangle path. Separator points between the signs are not part of any sign.

letters.variants: Compared by the independent checker (2026-10-20) with two other copies of the 1806 printing scanned for the Internet Archive: the Getty Research Institute copy (item ancientalphabets01ibnw, page image n190) and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill copy (item ancientalphabets00ibnw, page image n39), both Arabic p. 34, registered onto the Wellcome master and cut to the same cells. The form is the same in all three copies; the fork at the left end of the bar is clearest in the UNC copy. The book prints another table it gives to Hermes on Arabic p. 16, not traced here.
